- Risks and uncertainties:
  - Diversified generation and utilities operations across four SBUs, with exposure to renewables (wind, solar, storage).
  - Operating/economic risks in developing markets, transition away from fossil fuels, commodity and FX volatility, and potential revisions to thermal plant useful lives.
  - Financing risk from tighter credit markets; ratings at BBB- (S&P, Fitch) and Baa3 (Moody’s); potential downgrade could raise financing costs.
  - Liquidity noted with $1.4 billion unrestricted cash as of December 31, 2022.

structure.title: Earnings Per Share
structure.heading: Note 26 - Earnings Per Share
structure.summary:
- Earnings per share: AES reported losses from continuing operations in 2022 and 2021, leading basic and diluted EPS to be identical in those years; 2020 showed positive income with a modest dilutive impact from options and RSUs.
- Dilutive securities: For 2022 and 2021, 5 million stock awards and 40 million shares tied to March 2021 Equity Units were excluded from diluted EPS as anti-dilutive; had there been income, an estimated 3–4 million shares from awards and 33–40 million from Equity Units would have been included.
- Equity Units (issued March 2021): 10,430,500 Corporate Units (total notional $1.043 billion) each comprising a 2024 Purchase Contract and a 10% interest in one share of Series A Preferred Stock. Series A Preferred is convertible only upon a fundamental change before February 15, 2024, and freely thereafter; upon conversion, holders receive Series B Preferred or cash (in redemption cases) plus common shares for any value above liquidation preference. Initial conversion rate 31.5428 common shares per Series A Preferred (about $31.70 per share), adjusted to 31.5846 (about $31.66) by December 31, 2022. The Series A Preferred and 2024 Purchase Contracts are accounted for as one unit, and the if-converted method is used in diluted EPS considerations.
- Company profile: Diversified power generation and utility operations organized into four SBUs, with generation (coal, gas, hydro, wind, solar, biomass), utilities (transmission, distribution, and some generation), and growing renewables and energy storage.
- Operating and economic risks: Exposure to commodity and FX volatility, transition away from fossil fuels (potentially affecting plant useful lives), and tighter global credit markets. Investment-grade ratings (S&P and Fitch: BBB-; Moody’s: Baa3) and $1.4 billion in unrestricted cash as of December 31, 2022; potential adverse impact from any downgrade.
- International exposure: 68% of 2022 revenue generated outside the U.S., with significant operations in developing countries. Key risks include political/economic instability, hedging limitations, commodity and currency volatility, capital controls, regulatory and legal unpredictability, inflation, import restrictions, expropriation, contract enforceability challenges, adverse tax changes, and financing constraints.
- Regional volatility: Latin American operations subject to significant revenue and earnings swings due to regulatory/economic issues, political instability, PPA indexation to fuel prices, and currency fluctuations.
- Regulatory and tariff risks (especially for utilities): Potential adverse effects from inability to secure timely/adequate tariff adjustments and from changes in laws or interpretations affecting reimbursable cost definitions, controllable cost classifications, tax law, economic equilibrium provisions, concession determinations, timing of tariff increases, and environmental/greenhouse gas regulations.

structure.title: Risks and Uncertainties
structure.heading: Note 27 - Risks and Uncertainties
structure.start_phrase:
During 2022, 68% of our revenue was generated outside the U.S. and a significant portion of our international operations is conducted in
developing countries.
structure.summary:
- International operations and risk factors: 68% of 2022 revenue generated outside the U.S.; significant exposure to developing markets with risks including political/economic instability, commodity and currency volatility, inflation, contract enforceability challenges, regulatory/tax changes, import restrictions, financing constraints, and potential expropriation. Noted volatility in Latin America affecting revenues, margins, and cash flow predictability.
- Regulatory and tariff risk: Potential adverse impacts from changes in cost classifications, tax law, tariff timing/adjustments, economic equilibrium definitions, concession determinations, and environmental/GHG regulations, particularly in utility businesses.
- COVID-19: Ongoing uncertainty about magnitude/duration and possible adverse future effects on results, condition, and cash flows.
- Alto Maipo: 2021 Chapter 11 filing led to deconsolidation and a ~$1.2 billion after-tax loss; emerged from bankruptcy in May 2022. Post-emergence treated as a VIE; AES is not the primary beneficiary and elected fair value accounting; debt remains non-recourse to AES.
- Foreign currency risk: Earnings and cash flows sensitive to fluctuations in the Argentine peso, Brazilian real, Chilean peso, Colombian peso, Dominican peso, Euro, Indian rupee, and Mexican peso.
- Concentration and counterparty risk: Dependence on PPAs with limited customers at certain generation businesses, though no single customer represented ≥10% of total revenue in 2022–2020; exposure to customer/supplier credit quality and contract continuity.
- Related party transactions: Dealings with government-affiliated entities in Panama and the Dominican Republic, Mexican offtakers with board influence, and Fluence construction projects. 2022 P&L with related parties included non-regulated revenue ($1,093M), non-regulated cost of sales ($352M), interest income ($10M), and interest expense ($95M). Balance sheet included receivables ($484M), payables ($1,264M), and construction in progress ($714M). Noted $1B debt to Mong Duong Finance Holdings B.V. (equity affiliate SPV).
- Quarterly financial data (unaudited): 2022 and 2021 quarterly revenues, operating margins, EPS, and dividends presented, reflecting restatements for discontinued operations. Highlights include significant impairment charges in multiple quarters, a $777M goodwill impairment in 4Q22, other non-operating expense in 4Q22, and a 4Q21 loss on sale tied to Alto Maipo deconsolidation.
- Subsequent events: sPower sell-down of OpCo B on February 28, 2023 for $196M; AES ownership reduced from 50% to ~26%; equity method investment within US and Utilities SBU.
- Controls and procedures: Management concluded disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December 31, 2022. Management assessed internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) as effective under COSO 2013; Ernst & Young LLP issued an unqualified opinion on ICFR. No material changes to ICFR in 4Q22; no changes/disagreements with accountants; other required disclosures noted as none or not applicable.
- Governance and compensation (incorporated by reference): Director/executive info, code of ethics, audit committee, executive compensation, security ownership, related party policies, and auditor fees to be provided in the 2023 Proxy Statement.
- Equity compensation plans: Summary of securities authorized/available under stock plans as of December 31, 2022, including outstanding options/rights and remaining shares available; description of the 2003 Long Term Compensation Plan (as amended) and the director deferred compensation plan, and composition of outstanding PSU/RSU/DSU/options.
